_meta.indication: XOFLUZA is indicated for the treatment of acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 12 years of age and older who have been symptomatic for no more than 48 hours.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active (oseltamivir) and placebo-controlled trial in subjects 12 to 64 years of age; subjects 20 to 64 years were randomized 2:2:1 to a single weight-based dose of baloxavir marboxil (40 or 80 mg), oseltamivir 75 mg BID for 5 days, or placebo, while subjects 12 to <20 years were randomized 2:1 to weight-based baloxavir marboxil or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Otherwise healthy patients 12 to 64 years of age with acute uncomplicated influenza who were symptomatic for no more than 48 hours, enrolled in Japan, the US and Canada.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to alleviation of influenza symptoms, comparing baloxavir marboxil vs. placebo (Intent-to-Treat-Infected population).
pivotal_trials.n: 1436 randomized (612 baloxavir, 310 placebo, 514 oseltamivir); primary ITTI analysis N=456 baloxavir and N=231 placebo.
pivotal_trials.result: Median time to alleviation of symptoms 53.7 hours (95% CI 49.5, 58.5) with baloxavir vs. 80.2 hours (95% CI 72.6, 87.1) with placebo; difference -26.5 hours (95% CI -35.8, -17.8); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Adverse events were infrequent; in the pivotal trials only diarrhea (3%) and bronchitis (2%) were reported in ≥2% of baloxavir subjects, with diarrhea (3%) the only adverse drug reaction reported in >2% of the baloxavir arm.
target_moa: Baloxavir marboxil is a prodrug converted by hydrolysis to baloxavir, which inhibits the influenza virus polymerase acidic (PA) protein endonuclease, blocking viral mRNA transcription and viral RNA synthesis; a novel mechanism of action.
modality: Small molecule (oral prodrug converted to active baloxavir).

rems.type: No safety issues were identified to necessitate a REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee or other external consultations were held to discuss this application.
